insight.title: The CEO Who Bet the Rent on a Board Game
insight.subtitle: Reed Hastings had a failing DVD-by-mail startup until he chose to kill his best-performing product.
insight.notificationHook: Why Netflix killed its cash cow.

sections.text: By 2007, Netflix was a profitable DVD-by-mail powerhouse. But Reed Hastings saw a future in streaming, a technology that was still buffering, pixelated, and technically inferior to the discs that paid their bills.

In a closed-door meeting, he made the call to cannibalize his own business. He shifted focus to an unproven streaming model, effectively setting his primary revenue stream on a slow path to obsolescence.
The pivot caused the company’s stock to crater and ignited a massive customer revolt. Shareholders called him reckless; the industry assumed he had finally lost his grip on the market reality.
Sometimes, you have to destroy your success to survive the future.
